findings.trigger: Two distinct bank tenants submit independent case creation or transaction requests using identical client-generated idempotency keys (e.g., UUID 'idem-req-001').
findings.source_representation: Tenant A request with key 'idem-req-001' and Tenant B request with key 'idem-req-001'.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Tenant-scoped Redis keys 'idem:bank_a:idem-req-001' and 'idem:bank_b:idem-req-001', preserving total cross-tenant isolation.
findings.actual_representation: Global key 'idem:idem-req-001' shared across all institutions in the multi-tenant consortium.
findings.root_cause: _build_redis_key ignored tenant_id and formatted key as f'idem:{key_hash}', allowing cross-tenant key collisions, false HTTP 409 conflicts, and cross-tenant response payload leakage.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: All idempotent endpoints (e.g. /api/v1/cases/, transaction submission) when deployed in multi-tenant SaaS mode.
findings.tenant_impact: Direct cross-tenant collision and unauthorized visibility into another bank's cached response headers and body.
findings.temporal_impact: Cache collision persists for TTL duration (typically 86,400 seconds).
findings.proof: test_tenant_idempotency_isolation asserts that Bank A and Bank B acquiring the same idempotency key succeed concurrently without collision.
findings.repair: Updated IdempotencyService._build_redis_key to namespace keys with f'idem:{tenant_id}:{key_hash}' when tenant_id is provided, and updated cases.py to extract and pass tenant_id from auth context.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: No impact on offline FL model training benchmarks; affects live SaaS multi-tenant case creation and payment ingestion.

findings.trigger: Real-time transaction prediction requests received via /api/v1/predict/ with distinct customer or account identities.
findings.source_representation: Incoming TransactionPredictRequest containing payload with specific customer_id or account_id.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Feature store and rate limiter bind to entity_hash derived from actual customer/account identifier: f'{bank_id}:{customer_id}'.
findings.actual_representation: Hardcoded entity_hash = f'serving:{bank_id}:customer_1' regardless of the actual transacting entity.
findings.root_cause: Prediction router hardcoded 'customer_1' string instead of dynamically inspecting payload fields.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: FeatureStoreService sliding window aggregations (velocity_1h, velocity_24h, avg_amount_24h) for all customer transactions were conflated into a single customer profile per bank.
findings.tenant_impact: Severe entity conflation within the institution, causing false-positive fraud velocity triggers across distinct customers.
findings.temporal_impact: Persistent profile corruption across the sliding 24-hour window.
findings.proof: test_prediction_request_entity_identity verifies that customer_id and account_id are faithfully accepted and bound to feature store ingestion.
findings.repair: Added optional customer_id and account_id to TransactionPredictRequest schema, updated predict.py to resolve entity_hash dynamically from customer_id or account_id, and passed transaction_id to background feature ingestion.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: Affects real-time serving feature store profiles; offline batch benchmarks derived profiles directly from tabular dataset columns.

findings.trigger: Adversarial or corrupted upstream payload containing float('inf'), float('-inf'), or float('nan') in amount or feature fields.
findings.source_representation: JSON payload {'amount': 1e309} (deserializes to inf) or NaN.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Validation error (Pydantic ValidationError) rejecting non-finite floats at the ingestion boundary.
findings.actual_representation: Accepted silently because standard 'x > 0' check evaluates to True for float('inf').
findings.root_cause: Validation logic lacked math.isfinite() checks on numeric fields across NormalizedTransaction and TransactionPredictRequest.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: Graph edge weights, feature store sliding averages, and neural network inference poisoned by NaN/Inf propagations.
findings.tenant_impact: Local to bank sending corrupted record, but could destabilize shared graph algorithms.
findings.temporal_impact: Permanent until window expiration or node eviction.
findings.repair: Added math.isfinite validation to NormalizedTransaction.amount and all float fields in TransactionPredictRequest.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: Directly reinforces Phase 5D inference protections by halting non-finite values at the earlier ingestion boundary.

findings.trigger: Core banking or payment rail connector ingests historical or asynchronous transaction events.
findings.source_representation: Source messages with explicit execution timestamps: ISO 20022 CreDtTm/ValDt, Mambu creationDate, Thought Machine value_timestamp, SWIFT tag 32A.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: NormalizedTransaction.timestamp faithfully preserves the source event execution instant in UTC.
findings.actual_representation: NormalizedTransaction.timestamp was unconditionally overwritten with datetime.now(timezone.utc).
findings.root_cause: Connectors instantiated NormalizedTransaction with timestamp=datetime.now(timezone.utc) rather than parsing the explicit source timestamp attributes.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: Completely broke historical replay, batch backfilling, temporal graph analytics, and out-of-order event handling.
findings.tenant_impact: All institutions utilizing core banking or ISO 20022 connectors.
findings.temporal_impact: Destruction of original event time semantics across all downstream consumers.
findings.proof: test_iso20022_event_time_preservation, test_mambu_event_time_preservation, and test_thought_machine_event_time_preservation verify parsed source timestamp retention.
findings.repair: Implemented ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 datetime parsing across ISO 20022 (pacs.008, pain.001, camt.053, SWIFT MT103), Mambu, and Thought Machine connectors with fallback to now() only when source field is missing.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: No impact on historical static benchmark files; critical for live banking connectors and replay fidelity.

findings.trigger: Runtime configuration specifies connector_type as 'mambu', 'thought_machine', or 'kafka_streaming'.
findings.source_representation: Bank configuration with supported connector identifier present in CONNECTOR_REGISTRY.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Instantiates and returns the corresponding operational connector instance.
findings.actual_representation: Threw ValueError(f'Unsupported connector type: {connector_type}') despite being listed in supported registry.
findings.root_cause: Missing if/elif branches in BankConnectorFactory.get_connector dispatch method for registered core banking and streaming connectors.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: Core banking connectors and streaming Kafka pipelines were unreachable via standard factory dispatch.
findings.tenant_impact: Institutions configured with modern core banking or streaming engines could not initialize ingestion.
findings.proof: test_connector_factory_resolution verifies successful factory instantiation for all registered connector types.
findings.repair: Added explicit instantiation branches for 'mambu', 'thought_machine'/'thoughtmachine', and 'kafka_streaming'/'cloudevents' in factory.py.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: None on model training; enables production core banking connectors.

findings.trigger: Rapid concurrent delivery of duplicate messages across worker threads or network retries.
findings.source_representation: Two identical event deliveries arriving within a millisecond window.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Exactly one event acquires processing lock; duplicate is atomically detected and discarded.
findings.actual_representation: Check-then-act race condition allowed both threads to observe is_duplicate=False before either marked the key as processed.
findings.root_cause: IdempotencyEngine lacked atomic check-and-set locking, and checked duplicate status separately from marking processed.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: Duplicate publication of CloudEvents to output topics and duplicate downstream graph edge creations.
findings.tenant_impact: Spurious duplicate events under high-concurrency streaming ingest.
findings.temporal_impact: Transient race condition during network re-deliveries.
findings.proof: test_kafka_connector_concurrent_deduplication runs 20 concurrent threads attempting to process the same event ID, proving exactly one succeeds.
findings.repair: Added threading.Lock and atomic try_acquire(key) method to IdempotencyEngine, scoped keys by tenant, and ensured immediate acquisition.

findings.trigger: Canonical NormalizedTransaction dictionary passed to StreamingGraphService.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Directed edge created from account_id to counterparty_account_id in the MultiDiGraph.
findings.actual_representation: Silently skipped transaction because service looked only for legacy keys 'sender_id' or 'source_owner'.
findings.root_cause: Schema divergence between canonical NormalizedTransaction and internal graph ingestion adapter.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: Streaming graph remained completely empty when ingesting canonical transactions from ISO 20022 and core banking connectors.
findings.tenant_impact: Zero graph features or mule ring detection for connector-sourced transactions.
findings.proof: test_streaming_graph_direction_preservation verifies that account_id and counterparty_account_id create directed edges with correct attributes.
findings.repair: Updated add_transaction to inspect 'account_id' and 'counterparty_account_id' alongside legacy aliases.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: Connects Phase 5E graph engine to real-world connector ingestion pipelines.

findings.trigger: Missing amount fields or retried duplicate transaction ingestion into feature store sliding window.
findings.source_representation: Transactions re-ingested after network retry, or records with missing amount fields.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Missing amount rejected as invalid; retried duplicate transactions deduplicated by tx_id without incrementing velocity.
findings.actual_representation: Connectors fabricated default amount=0.0 on missing amounts, and feature store appended duplicates into window list, doubling velocity counts.
findings.root_cause: Permissive fallbacks ('amount or 0.0') and lack of transaction_id deduplication in feature store sliding window deque.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: Spurious fraud risk score spikes on legitimate transactions due to network retries inflating velocity_1h and velocity_24h.
findings.tenant_impact: Elevated false positive rate during network instability.
findings.temporal_impact: Persists for duration of the 1h and 24h sliding windows.
findings.proof: test_feature_store_retry_deduplication verifies that duplicate ingest of the same tx_id maintains invariant velocity_1h count.
findings.repair: Removed zero-amount fallbacks in connectors to enforce strict positive amounts, added transaction_id tracking to FeatureStoreService, and deduplicated sliding window entries by tx_id.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: Ensures mathematical invariance of velocity features under network retries.

findings.trigger: Out-of-order or future-dated transaction ingestion into FeatureStore sliding window.
findings.source_representation: Transactions with timestamp ts > current_time + 300s, or out-of-order events where future records leaked into historical window queries.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Future-dated records > 300s rejected as clock-skew violations; sliding window queries strictly bounded within [ts - W, ts].
findings.actual_representation: Sliding window filtered using 'tx.timestamp >= one_hour_ago' without upper bound '<= ts', allowing future events to leak into past velocity features, with zero clock-skew rejection.
findings.root_cause: Missing upper bound check '<= ts' on window filtering deque, and missing clock-skew boundary check against system UTC time.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: Historical replay calculations and out-of-order streaming events polluted historical customer velocity profiles.
findings.tenant_impact: Distorted risk scoring for replayed or out-of-order transaction streams.
findings.temporal_impact: Lookahead data leakage during out-of-order processing.
findings.proof: test_sliding_window_recomputation_oracle and test_feature_store_clock_skew_tolerance prove strict window bounds and rejection of skew > 300s.
findings.repair: Enforced strict one_hour_ago <= tx.timestamp <= ts filtering in sliding window and added immediate return rejection for ts > now + 300.0s.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: Prevents temporal lookahead leakage during streaming simulation benchmarks.

findings.trigger: Independent banking institutions submit transactions with identical local customer IDs (e.g., 'cust_vip') or transaction IDs (e.g., 'tx_001').
findings.source_representation: Bank A transaction with customer_id='cust_vip' and Bank B transaction with customer_id='cust_vip'.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Feature store state namespaced by tenant (f'{tenant_id}:{customer_id}'), keeping customer velocity, profile, and history strictly disjoint.
findings.actual_representation: Global keys 'cust_vip' stored in Redis/memory, causing Bank B transactions to overwrite Bank A customer history and falsely trigger duplicate suppression.
findings.root_cause: FeatureStoreService lacked tenant_id parameter and stored un-scoped raw customer and merchant identifiers.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: Multi-tenant SaaS serving environments where separate banks use common account/customer numbering schemes.
findings.tenant_impact: Direct cross-tenant collision, profile pollution, and mutual denial-of-service via duplicate suppression.
findings.temporal_impact: Persistent across the sliding window duration (24 hours).
findings.proof: test_feature_store_cross_tenant_isolation verifies Bank A and Bank B maintain independent velocity and average amounts for identical IDs.
findings.repair: Added tenant_id parameter to ingest_transaction and get_online_features, namespacing all customer, merchant, and transaction keys by tenant.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: Essential for multi-tenant consortium deployments; offline datasets had distinct bank IDs.

findings.trigger: Client reuses an existing Idempotency-Key with a conflicting or altered mutation payload (e.g., amount changed from 100 to 900).
findings.source_representation: Request 1: key='idem_1', payload={'amount': 100}; Request 2: key='idem_1', payload={'amount': 900}.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: HTTP 409 Conflict rejection ('MISMATCH') notifying caller of conflicting payload under reused key.
findings.actual_representation: IdempotencyService returned the cached 200 response from Request 1, silently ignoring the conflicting payload in Request 2.
findings.root_cause: IdempotencyService stored only the response body without binding a cryptographic hash of the request payload.
findings.downstream_blast_radius: API endpoints using idempotency keys (cases router, resource creation).
findings.tenant_impact: Silent masking of contradictory business mutations.
findings.temporal_impact: Persists for the 24-hour idempotency TTL window.
findings.proof: test_idempotency_conflicting_payload verifies that matching payload returns HIT and conflicting payload returns MISMATCH.
findings.repair: Added payload_hash support to IdempotencyService envelope; acquire returns MISMATCH on hash discrepancy, and cases router returns HTTP 409 Conflict.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: No impact on ML benchmarks; protects operational API integrity.

findings.trigger: Multiple distributed Kafka consumer workers process duplicate messages concurrently across separate Python processes.
findings.source_representation: Two independent worker processes receive the same CloudEvent delivery.
findings.expected_canonical_representation: Shared distributed Redis atomic reservation (SET NX EX) guarantees exactly one worker processes the mutation.
findings.actual_representation: IdempotencyEngine used in-process threading.Lock, protecting threads within one process but not multiple distinct worker processes.
findings.root_cause: IdempotencyEngine was decoupled from distributed IdempotencyService.
findings.tenant_impact: Duplicate event processing across horizontally scaled workers during rebalances.
findings.proof: test_kafka_idempotency_semantics certifies acquire, duplicate detection, and release lifecycle.
findings.repair: Bridged IdempotencyEngine to IdempotencyService Redis backend when available, preserving robust thread-safe in-memory fallback.
findings.historical_evidence_relevance: Clarifies distributed vs in-process concurrency boundaries.
